R5 `isinstance(web_plugin_policy_evidence, WebPluginPolicyEvidence)` in `begin_run`, guarding the optional epoch-23 evidence argument before it reaches `_insert_web_plugin_policy_evidence`. This is nominal typing against a concrete frozen dataclass ELSPETH defines (`contracts/plugin_policy_audit.py`) - the exact mechanism ADR-032 Decision(1) prescribes for what ELSPETH owns - and it must be nominal rather than structural because the insert reads eleven attributes straight onto the `run_web_plugin_policy` audit table (`schema_version`, `policy_hash`, `snapshot_hash`, `binding_generation_fingerprint`, plus seven `canonical_json` columns). Any duck-typed object carrying those attribute names would be persisted as authentic policy evidence while bypassing `WebPluginPolicyEvidence.__post_init__`, which is where the sha256 digest shape, the kind-qualified plugin-id shape, the canonical sorted-unique ordering, and the `available_plugin_ids` subset-of `authorized_plugin_ids` invariant are actually enforced. So this is an admission gate on an audit table, not a shape guard hiding a caller bug: it raises `AuditIntegrityError` and fails the run closed at the write, and the `is not None` operand ahead of it keeps the CLI path (which passes None) out of scope. Honest gap to record: unlike the four `_parse_field_resolution_mapping` sites below, no test drives the raising branch - every caller in tests passes either None or a real `WebPluginPolicyEvidence` (tests/unit/engine/orchestrator/test_landscape_registration.py:78, tests/integration/test_adr_019_sweep_durability.py:185). It stops being right if the evidence insert stops reading attributes off a caller-supplied object - if `begin_run` took the already-validated column values, or reconstructed an owned `WebPluginPolicyEvidence` inside the repository, the construction becomes the gate and this line becomes redundant.

R5 `isinstance(resolution_data, dict)` in `_parse_field_resolution_mapping`, applied to the value returned by `json.loads(resolution_json)` two lines above. The flagged subject is a parse result, not a first-party typed value: `json.loads` returns any JSON type, so a stored `null`, `[]` or `42` deserialises to None/list/int and the `"resolution_mapping" not in resolution_data` membership test and the `resolution_data[...]` subscript immediately below would raise a bare `TypeError` naming neither the run nor the corrupt column. Narrowing a parse result before use is ADR-032 Decision(2) applied to the one input this method has. The row comes from our own Landscape audit store, so the correct outcome is a crash and it crashes: `AuditIntegrityError` naming run_id, location and the observed type - the discrimination an operator needs to tell database corruption from a writer defect. Both arms are pinned adversarially against a deliberately corrupted column: tests/unit/core/landscape/test_run_lifecycle_repository.py `TestGetSourceFieldResolution::test_corrupt_non_dict_json_raises` (stored `"just a string"`) and `::test_corrupt_array_json_raises` (stored `[1, 2, 3]`). It stops being right if `record_source_field_resolution` stops storing a free-form JSON document and the column becomes a structured surface whose shape the database itself enforces.

R5 `isinstance(resolution_mapping, dict)` in `_parse_field_resolution_mapping`, applied to `resolution_data["resolution_mapping"]`. This is not a duplicate of the guard on the enclosing document at line 1361: proving the document is a dict says nothing about the type of any value inside it, and JSON object values are unconstrained - the stored key may hold a string, a list, or null. Without this narrowing the `.items()` loop below raises `AttributeError` on a str/list/None and reports the corruption as an unrelated crash instead of an audit-integrity failure carrying run_id, location and the observed type. Tier-1 store, so it fails closed with `AuditIntegrityError` rather than substituting an empty default - a silently-empty resolution mapping would let a resume replay under the wrong header normalisation, which is the failure this method exists to prevent. Pinned adversarially by tests/unit/core/landscape/test_run_lifecycle_repository.py `TestGetSourceFieldResolution::test_resolution_mapping_not_dict_raises`, which stores `{"resolution_mapping": "not a dict"}` and asserts the raise. It stops being right if the writer's payload gains a schema check at the storage boundary that makes the inner value's type a database-enforced fact.

R5 `isinstance(key, str)` in `_parse_field_resolution_mapping`'s per-entry validation loop - the first operand of the `str->str` check. Declared defense-in-depth, and both the production comment above the line and the docstring of tests/unit/core/landscape/test_run_lifecycle_repository.py `TestGetSourceFieldResolution::test_non_string_value_raises` say so explicitly: `json.loads` with the default decoder always produces `str` keys, so against today's single producer this operand cannot evaluate False, and the test deliberately exercises only the VALUE operand. It is kept rather than deleted because it is the only check that would catch a non-string key if this stored document were ever rehydrated by anything other than the stdlib JSON decoder (an `object_pairs_hook`, msgpack, or a direct row-to-dict path), and the loop is what builds the `dict[str, str]` this method returns to the resume header path. This file already keeps one such branch on the same footing - `::test_non_string_schema_raises` is skipped with the reason 'SQLite type affinity coerces int->str in TEXT columns; branch unreachable with SQLite backend', i.e. the branch is held for stricter backends. It costs one branch on a resume-path read and fails closed with `AuditIntegrityError` naming both observed types. Reported honestly as the weakest of this file's five sites: unlike its line-mates its necessity is an inference about deserialisers, not a fact about the code as written. Two changes invalidate it - pinning `json.loads` as the enforced and only deserialiser for this column, at which point it is provably dead and should be DELETED rather than re-justified; or a change to the method's `dict[str, str]` return contract.

R5 `isinstance(value, str)` in `_parse_field_resolution_mapping`'s per-entry validation loop - the second operand of the `str->str` check, and unlike its key-side line-mate it is live against the current producer. JSON object VALUES are unconstrained, so a stored mapping entry may hold a number, a list, an object or null; this operand is the only thing standing between such a value and `validated_mapping[key] = value`, which the method returns as `dict[str, str]` and whose callers use to rename source headers on resume. Admitting a non-string here would corrupt header resolution silently at resume time, far from the read that introduced it, instead of failing at the read. Tier-1 audit store, therefore fail closed: `AuditIntegrityError` naming run, location and the observed key and value types. Pinned adversarially twice over in tests/unit/core/landscape/test_run_lifecycle_repository.py `TestGetSourceFieldResolution` - `::test_non_string_value_raises` (stored `{"header": 42}`) and `::test_non_string_null_value_raises` (stored `{"header": null}`), the null case mattering because a bare truthiness test would let it through. It stops being right if the resolution mapping stops being a flat str->str document - if a future format nests a per-field record, this method needs a real parser and this operand must be replaced rather than widened.
